title: A write while the tournament is run from a laptop (contract revision 7)
description: While a tournament's `relay` is not null, this server holds a mirror and the laptop decides. Every write the app makes on that tournament (POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE under /tournaments/:id, apart from the app's own presence, handover notes, push registration and sign-out) is not done here: it is sent to the laptop, which runs it through its own copy of this API under the role the app has here, so every check, question and refusal is the desk's own. The write is answered `202` with `state: pending`. Send an `Idempotency-Key` header with every write (a UUID the app keeps with it): the same key again is the same command, answered with where it stands (`200` once answered, `202` while still pending), never a second one; without a key every send is a new command. Ask `GET /tournaments/:id/commands/:cid` (`cid` is the key) for the answer, or resend; the change itself shows up in the tournament's ordinary answers once the laptop has made it. `accepted`: the laptop made it; `status` is what its API answered, `response` its body for the writes whose body the app reads (board link, live board, hall commands, line-up check). `refused`: `error` and `message` are what the laptop's API refused with (`status` its HTTP status), `response` the rest of that refusal - `confirm`, `summary`, `warnings` on 409 needs_acknowledgement (ask, and send the write again with `acknowledged` and a NEW key), `current` on a conflict. The server itself refuses before sending: 404 not_found (a row the laptop never had), 409 desk_only (an Undo of a change made before the laptop took over), 400 bad_request (a write the laptop cannot run). A tournament's writes are answered as before (200, 201, 204) whenever `relay` is null. On the hall path (revision 8, `relay.hall`) the laptop runs the write at once and answers `200` with this shape, `accepted` or `refused`, never `pending`; the same `Idempotency-Key` is the same command on the laptop and on this server alike, so the laptop's answer to a write is the answer this server gives for it once the laptop has spoken, whichever path it went by first. GET /tournaments/:id/commands/:cid on the laptop answers the same way.

cid.description: The Idempotency-Key the write was sent with, or one the server made up.

action.description: Which write, e.g. player.update, round_edit.edit, tournament.publish, match.set_lineups.

status.description: The HTTP status the laptop's API answered; null while pending.

error.description: refused only: the error code, as error.schema.json's `error`. Two are this server's own, set without the laptop and with `status` and `message` null: relay_stopped (the laptop stopped relaying, or handed the tournament back, before it ran the command) and, from contract revision 9, laptop_lost (the tournament was taken back here without the laptop; the command was never run and will not be: the arbiter sees it listed and does it at the desk if it is still wanted). One is the laptop's own rather than its API's: interrupted (status 503; the laptop stopped while it ran the command, which may or may not have been done; it is not run again, so check at the laptop before sending a new one).

message.description: refused only: the sentence to show.
